chore: upgrade to TypeScript 6 (#21786)

## Background

- TypeScript 6 is the next step toward TypeScript 7. It checks several
byte and stream types more strictly than TypeScript 5.
- Earlier PRs prepared the repository for this upgrade:
- [Remove `baseUrl` from TypeScript
configs](https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/21482). TypeScript 6
deprecates this option.
- [Move from `tsup` to
`tsdown`](https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/21642). The build tool now
supports newer TypeScript versions.
- The SDK must keep its public types, bundles, and runtime behavior
during this compiler upgrade.

## Summary

- Upgrade TypeScript to 6.0.3.
- Fix several type errors without assertions:
- When `generateText` downloads a file returned by a model, it keeps the
bytes in a map so it can reuse them later in the call. Give that map the
type its download helper expects.
- Let functions that encode text or decode base64 keep their inferred
return types. Explicit `Uint8Array` return types hide the more precise
buffer type from TypeScript.
- Add assertions where TypeScript 6 rejects values that the code already
passes to Web APIs:
- **Blob inputs:** File uploads, transcription audio, images, and
downloaded files use byte arrays with `new Blob(...)`. TypeScript 6
requires a narrower backing-buffer type for those arrays. Assert them as
`Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>` at each Blob call. The calls continue to use
the same byte arrays.
- **Tool-approval secret:** `crypto.subtle.importKey` requires the same
narrower byte-array type as Blob. Assert the supplied `Uint8Array`
secret at the call site. The public secret type stays the same.
- **Realtime frame:** WebSocket sends require the same narrower
backing-buffer type. After `ArrayBuffer.isView` identifies a view,
assert it as `ArrayBufferView<ArrayBuffer>`. The frame keeps the
original view and byte count.
- **Text decoding:** TypeScript 6 gives `TextDecoderStream` a narrower
input type than our existing byte streams. Assert the decoder’s stream
type where core, provider utilities, and harness pipe bytes through it.
The decoding steps stay the same.
- **Fetch body:** `postToApi` accepts strings, form data, byte arrays,
and Blobs. Fetch requires the same narrower byte-array type as Blob.
Assert the body at the `fetch` call so callers can continue to pass the
existing types.
- **Test-server response:** Binary test fixtures use Node `Buffer`,
while mock service worker types `HttpResponse.arrayBuffer` as accepting
`ArrayBuffer`. Assert the fixture body as `ArrayBuffer` through
`unknown`. This keeps the body passed to MSW unchanged.

feat(harness-pi): keep the Pi session in lifecycle data, with an optional session storage (#23370)

## Background

The Pi adapter kept per-session state on the host and in the sandbox. At
session start it copied the sandbox workspace to the host and patched
Node's `fs` module process-wide to serve that copy at the sandbox path,
only so Pi's filesystem discovery could find `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`
and project skills. Stopping, detaching or suspending a session copied
Pi's session file into the sandbox, and resuming read it back from
there, so a conversation was tied to one sandbox and every lifecycle
step made sandbox calls. Pi runs in the host process, so this state is
shared by every session that process serves.

## Summary

- **No workspace mirror.** The mirror, the `fs` patch and the host probe
are deleted. Native file tools resolve paths against the sandbox work
directory, and `fileToolPathPolicy` roots are checked against sandbox
paths only, denied roots first. Pi reads no project settings, context
files or skills from the host.
- **`resources.skills`.** Skills that already exist in the sandbox are
listed to the model through this new setting and read with the `read`
tool. Skills passed to `HarnessAgent` keep working as before. Project
context goes in `instructions`.
- **Sandbox paths resolved on first use.** The sandbox `HOME`, canonical
denied roots, path mapper and remote ops are resolved the first time a
native file tool runs or a turn has skills to write, and retried on the
next use if that fails. Skills that an earlier process wrote and the
current turn no longer passes are removed through the `writeSkills`
manifest the first time a native tool uses the sandbox, once per
process. Pi's session start makes no sandbox calls, and neither does a
turn that never touches the sandbox.
- **Session in lifecycle data.** One in-memory Pi `SessionManager` owns
the session. The `data` of both lifecycle states is now `{ entries,
pendingToolBatch? }`: the Pi session header and entries, plus the tool
batch that was waiting on host input. Nothing about the session is
stored in the sandbox or on the host, so a continuation can run in any
process and any sandbox. When a batch is waiting on host input, the
entries are captured before the turn is aborted, as before.
- **Rebuilds keep the conversation.** Rebuilding the Pi session for a
changed tool set used to start it with an empty history.
- **Optional session storage.** `createPi({ sessionStorage })` takes a
caller-provided append-only log per session (`PiSessionStorage`).
`append({ sessionId, entry })` adds one entry `{ entryId, parentEntryId,
version, data }`: a Pi session entry keyed by Pi's own entry id and its
parent's id, with the Pi session version it was written under. `read({
sessionId, leafId })` returns those entries for the path that leads to
`leafId` in append order (returning every entry is also valid), and the
harness uses their `version` and `data`. A storage that implements the
optional `appendMany({ sessionId, entries })` receives a stop's new
entries in one call; without it, the harness calls `append` once per
entry. All three take an optional `abortSignal`. The state's `data`
holds only `{ leafId, pendingToolBatch? }`, so it stays small however
long the session grows (image-heavy sessions were passing the 50 MB
workflow step limit). Pi entries form a tree, so a regenerated turn, a
retried step or a second turn resumed from the same state appends a new
branch, and each state's `leafId` selects its own; nothing is
overwritten. An entry whose `entryId` the log already holds is a retried
append and can be ignored. `version` is its own field, like
durable-harness's `v` on each journal record, because a read of one
branch never includes a session header to migrate by; `data` is the
plain Pi entry, typed as Pi's `SessionEntry`. Without a storage, the
state holds the whole session as before, and the entries of a state
recorded without one are appended on the next stop.

### Behavior changes for existing users

- A lifecycle state recorded before this version (`{ sessionFileName }`)
still validates but resumes as a fresh session, so conversations
suspended across the upgrade lose their history. A pending tool batch in
such a state is dropped.
- Pi no longer picks up `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` or project skills from
the sandbox workspace on its own. Use `instructions` and
`resources.skills`.
- Inline extensions no longer see a host copy of the workspace. They
read project files through `session.sandboxSession`.
- A denied root that cannot be resolved fails the native file tool call
that needs it instead of failing session start.

## Manual Verification

Run against the real Pi runtime through `HarnessAgent` with Claude Haiku
4.5 over the AI Gateway, with a local just-bash sandbox.

- A chat-only turn: Pi made no sandbox call. The only calls were
`HarnessAgent`'s own work directory `mkdir` and `onSession`.
- A turn that runs `bash` returned the command's output, and with
`fileToolPathPolicy: { writableRoots: ['/tmp/pi-out'] }` the `write`
tool created the file there with the requested content.
- Told the model a codename, stopped the session, and resumed it from
the lifecycle state with a new `HarnessAgent` in a brand-new sandbox.
The state carried six entries and no `sessionFileName`, and the model
answered with the codename.
- Ran 31 of the 35 examples in
`examples/ai-functions/src/harness-agent/pi/` with the Vercel sandbox

feat(elevenlabs): streaming speech over WebSocket; type v4/v3-conversational model ids (#23795)

## Background

Stacked on `experimental_streamSpeech`. ElevenLabs serves streaming TTS
over the text-to-speech WebSocket
(`/v1/text-to-speech/{voice_id}/stream-input`), which accepts text
incrementally, so it is a natural first implementation of
`Experimental_StreamingSpeechModelV4`. `elevenlabs.speech()` is
unchanged; `ElevenLabsSpeechModel` now implements the streaming
extension.

## Summary

- `ElevenLabsSpeechModel.doStream()`:
- opens `wss://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/text-to-speech/{voice}/stream-input`
with `model_id`, `output_format`, and the optional query settings
(`language_code`, `enable_logging`, `inactivity_timeout`,
`sync_alignment`, `auto_mode`, `apply_text_normalization`, `seed`,
`enable_ssml_parsing`)
- sends the init message (`text: " "`, `voice_settings`,
`generation_config.chunk_length_schedule`,
`pronunciation_dictionary_locators`, and the API key as `xi-api-key`),
text messages, then `{"text":""}`
- **auth in the first message**, not a header, so the native `WebSocket`
works in every runtime; the key is kept out of the reported
`request.body`
- **text parts**: the stream-input socket speaks one voice, so a part
whose `voice` differs from the call's voice errors the stream
(`InvalidArgumentError`)
- **word-boundary buffering**: ElevenLabs expects each text message to
end at whitespace, and LLM deltas often split words, so partial words
are held back until the next whitespace (CJK sentence punctuation also
counts; capped at 100 held code points for unspaced scripts) and the
rest is flushed at end of input
- **keepalives**: `{"text":" "}` after 15 s without a send, so a slow
text producer (e.g. a reasoning model) does not hit the server's default
20 s inactivity timeout. None after end of input; an explicit
`inactivityTimeout` turns them off so the timeout you set applies.
Verified live that whitespace-only keepalives are not billed.
- **output format**: the portable `outputFormat` maps to an ElevenLabs
`output_format` (`audio/mpeg` 44.1/22.05 kHz, `audio/pcm` 8–48 kHz with
24 kHz default, `audio/pcmu` / `audio/pcma` 8 kHz, `audio/opus` /
`audio/ogg` 48 kHz); anything else is rejected. `streaming.outputFormat`
takes a native format (e.g. `mp3_44100_192`). Default `mp3_44100_128`.
Each mapping was checked live on the WebSocket; Opus arrives in an Ogg
container, so it is reported as `audio/ogg`.
- emits `audio` parts (base64, with `audioFormat` derived from
`output_format`, and `alignment` / `normalizedAlignment` in
`providerMetadata.elevenlabs`), and `finish` on `isFinal` with
`usage.inputCharacters` = Unicode code points sent
- surfaces server error messages and early closes (with close
code/reason) as stream errors; closes the socket and cancels the text
stream on cancel/abort
- New `providerOptions.elevenlabs.streaming`: `autoMode`,
`chunkLengthSchedule`, `enableSsmlParsing`, `inactivityTimeout`,
`outputFormat`, `syncAlignment`. Options the WebSocket doesn't support
(`previousText`, `nextText`, `previousRequestIds`, `nextRequestIds`,
`applyLanguageTextNormalization`, `instructions`) produce warnings.
- `eleven_v3*` / `eleven_v4*` ids reject `doStream` with
`UnsupportedFunctionalityError` (the stream-input WebSocket does not
serve them).
- The speech model now receives the provider's `webSocket` setting
(previously transcription only); it is optional, since auth rides the
first message.
- Streaming requires versioned pronunciation dictionary locators (the
WebSocket rejects unversioned ones); this is validated before
connecting.
- `doGenerate` ignores `providerOptions.elevenlabs.streaming` with an
`unsupported` warning (it applies only to streaming speech).
- Typed model ids: `eleven_v4`, `eleven_v4_turbo`,
`eleven_v3_conversational`.
- Docs: "Streaming Speech Models" section on the ElevenLabs provider
page; the capability table gains a Streaming Speech column (and no
longer claims `instructions` support, which the provider ignores with a
warning). Examples: `stream-speech/elevenlabs/basic.ts` and
`stream-text.ts` (pipes a `streamText` text stream into `streamSpeech`).

WebSocket to `doStream` through `providerOptions.elevenlabs.dialogue`.

`providerOptions.elevenlabs.dialogue: { voices, voiceSettings?: {
stability } }` with an `eleven_v3*` / `eleven_v4*` model.

`voice`, else the first dialogue voice). Voices must be listed in
`dialogue.voices`, because the socket needs them in its first message;
an unlisted voice errors at once (on the call `voice`, before
connecting). A voice change starts a new turn (`new_turn`);
`providerOptions: { elevenlabs: { newTurn: true } }` on a part forces
one with the same voice.

speaker or turn changes; voices are resolved when a part is read, so
naming the default voice explicitly does not split a held word.
- `eleven_v4*`: text becomes `{ inputs: [{ text, voice_id, new_turn? }]
}` messages (word-boundary buffered, as for TTS), then `close_socket`.
- `eleven_v3*`: the server rejects incremental inputs (1008, re-checked
live), so the provider reads the whole text stream and sends a single `{
inputs, close_socket: true }`.
- `eleven_v3_conversational` supports exactly one voice; more are
rejected before connecting.
- Auth rides the first message (`xi_api_key`), and `{"keep_alive":true}`
is sent while the text stream is idle (also accepted by the v3 family
while it buffers). Text-to-Dialogue has a fixed 20 s timeout, so
keepalives stay on even with `inactivityTimeout` set.
- Snake_case server frames are normalized: `alignment` → camelCase
(`charStartTimesMs`, ...), `is_final` → finish. Standalone
`is_final_audio_for_turn` frames are emitted as metadata-only (empty)
audio parts with `providerMetadata.elevenlabs.isFinalAudioForTurn`.
- Refactor: `createElevenLabsSpeechStream` now takes a small protocol
object (init + auth fields / keepalive / resolve voice / encode text /
end / decode), shared by TTS and dialogue.
- Guards: dialogue on a non-v3/v4 model and v3/v4 without dialogue throw
before connecting. `doGenerate` ignores `dialogue` with a warning.
Options Text-to-Dialogue does not take (`speed`, top-level
`voiceSettings`, and the `autoMode` / `chunkLengthSchedule` /
`enableSsmlParsing` / `inactivityTimeout` streaming options) produce
warnings.

fix(elevenlabs): parse ElevenLabs error bodies so messages and request ids are preserved (#24141)

## Background

When an ElevenLabs request fails, the `APICallError` thrown by
`@ai-sdk/elevenlabs` (speech and transcription) has only the HTTP status
text as its message, e.g. `Bad Request` or `Not Found`. The error code,
the ElevenLabs message, and the request id are lost, and `error.data` is
`undefined`.

The cause is a schema mismatch. `elevenlabs-error.ts` expected `{ error:
{ message, code: number } }`, but ElevenLabs reports errors under
`detail`:

```json
{"detail":{"type":"not_found","code":"voice_not_found","message":"A voice with voice_id '…' was not found.","status":"voice_not_found","request_id":"…"}}
{"detail":[{"type":"missing","loc":["body","text"],"msg":"Field required","input":null}]}
```

Because the body never matched, `createJsonErrorResponseHandler` fell
back to `response.statusText`.

## Summary

- `elevenlabsErrorDataSchema` now accepts `detail` as an object
(`message` plus optional `code`, `status`, `type`, `request_id`,
`param`), a FastAPI-style validation array (`msg`, `loc`, `type`), or a
string. The legacy `{ error: { message, code } }` shape is still
accepted. The detail object and array entries are parsed loosely, so
every field in the response stays on `APICallError.data`.
- Error messages are built in this order:
- object detail: `<message> (<code>)`, or just `<message>` when there is
no code
  - array detail: `<loc joined by '.'>: <msg>`, joined with `; `
  - string detail: the string
  - legacy: `error.message`
- Both the speech and transcription models use this handler, so both are
fixed.

Tests that cover the fix (all of them fail on `main` with the old
schema):

- `elevenlabs-error.test.ts`: one case each for the object, array,
string, and legacy shapes, checking the message and that `request_id`
(and the rest of the body) survives in `APICallError.data`.
- `elevenlabs-speech-model.test.ts` › `should surface the ElevenLabs
error message and code`: a 404 `detail` body.
- `elevenlabs-transcription-model.test.ts` › `errors` › `should surface
the ElevenLabs error message and code`: a 404 `detail` body.

key (`abcdef`), once with `speech().doGenerate` and once with
`transcription().doGenerate`:

- before: `400 "Bad Request"`, with no `request_id` in `error.data`
- after: `400 "API key must start with 'sk_'. (invalid_api_key)"`, with
`error.data.detail.request_id` present

feat(ai): add experimental_streamSpeech (#23794)

## Background

Stacked on the provider-spec PR (`Experimental_StreamingSpeechModelV4`).
This adds the user-facing function.

## Summary

`experimental_streamSpeech` streams speech audio using models that
implement the experimental `Experimental_StreamingSpeechModelV4` (a
`SpeechModelV4` with `doStream()`). Models resolve as usual (string IDs
through the global provider) and are narrowed at runtime; a model that
cannot stream throws `UnsupportedFunctionalityError`:

```ts
const { textStream } = streamText({ model, prompt });

const result = experimental_streamSpeech({
  model: elevenLabs.speech('eleven_flash_v2_5'),
  text: textStream, // a string, or an array or stream of strings and/or text parts
  outputFormat: { type: 'audio/mpeg' },
});

for await (const chunk of result.audioStream) {
  // Uint8Array
}
console.log(await result.usage); // { inputCharacters: ... }
```

- `text` accepts a string, or an array / `Iterable` / `AsyncIterable` /
`ReadableStream` of strings and/or text parts
(`Experimental_SpeechTextPart`: `{ type: 'text', text, voice?,
providerOptions? }`); strings become text parts. Anything else throws
`InvalidArgumentError`.
- `outputFormat` is a `SharedV4AudioFormat` (`{ type, rate? }`), the
same shape as each chunk's `audioFormat`.
- Returns `audioStream` (bytes) and `fullStream` (`audio` parts with
`Uint8Array` audio + `audioFormat`, `raw`, `error`), sharing one live
single-consumer stream, plus `usage`, `warnings`, `responses`, and
`providerMetadata` promises. Same ownership rules as
`experimental_streamTranscribe`: no replay buffer, since text from an
LLM stream can be unbounded.
- Base64 audio chunks are decoded; empty chunks are dropped unless they
carry `providerMetadata` (e.g. a provider's end-of-turn marker), in
which case they appear in `fullStream` only.
- Provider `error` parts are non-fatal: `fullStream` passes them
through, `audioStream` skips them, and each goes to `onError` (default
`console.error`, not awaited).
- A stream that ends without audio rejects with `NoSpeechGeneratedError`
(the last `error` part is its `cause`); one that stops after audio but
before `finish` rejects with the last error part or a
`StreamProviderError`.
- Cancelling the output stream (`fullStream` or `audioStream`) or
aborting via `abortSignal` rejects pending result promises immediately
and aborts `doStream`, even if the provider ignores the signal; a
`doStream` rejection cancels the text stream too. `audioStream` is a
pull-based projection (no second `pipeThrough`), so early cancellation
does not surface an unhandled rejection.
- `responses` keeps the response `body` from `doStream` and from
`response-metadata` parts.
- No retries: the text stream is single-use.
- Docs: a "Streaming Speech" section in the Speech guide and an
`experimental_streamSpeech` reference page (with an Errors section).

Not included (follow-up): telemetry events for streaming speech
(transcription has `experimental_onStreamTranscription*`). Streaming
speech is v7 / spec v4 only; no v5/v6 backport is planned.

fix(harness-opencode): continue turns paused for a tool approval or tool result (#23331)

## Background

When OpenCode stops for a tool approval, `agent.continueStream()` does
not continue the turn. This occurs for Allow and for Deny. A host tool
result has the same problem.

The cause is the `pendingTurnDrain` wait in `prepareTurn`, from #21683.
For a continue, this drain belongs to the paused turn. The paused turn
cannot finish before it gets the answer. The host sends the answer only
after `doContinueTurn` returns. The result is a deadlock.

A session resumed with the `rerun` strategy has a second problem.
`rerunContinue` stays `true`. Each continue sends a new `start`, and the
bridge aborts the paused turn.

## Summary

- `doPromptTurn` waits for `pendingTurnDrain`. New prompts keep the
#21680 fix.
- `doContinueTurn` waits only for `abortedTurnDrain`. `onAbort` sets
this value.
- `doPromptTurn` and `doContinueTurn` set `rerunContinue` to `false`.
`harness-claude-code` and `harness-codex` use the same method.
- The new tests cover approval pauses, tool-result pauses, resumed
sessions, and a continue after an abort.

## End-to-End Verification

I ran the reproduction script from #23275 with OpenCode 1.18.34, a local
sandbox, and a mock model. I also ran it on a session resumed from
`session.stop()`.

- Before the fix, Allow and Deny do not continue (`HANG: no part from
continueStream after 30 s`).
- After the fix, Allow runs the command. Deny returns `tool-error`, and
the command does not run.
- The resumed session gives the same results. Without the
`rerunContinue` change, it does not continue.

fix: map `reasoning` consistently across providers (#24123)

## Background

AI SDK's top level `reasoning` option was mapped inconsistently across
providers.
- each provider implemented its own fallback logic. so some rounded up,
others rounded down
- handled unsupported `reasoning: 'none'` differently as well (some
dropped with warning, others silently, others sent through and API
rejected)
- didn't consistently prefer `providerOptions` reasoning

## Summary

Every provider now resolves reasoning with the same rule:

- **Provider options win.** A setting in `providerOptions` isn't
validated or rounded or dropped and is always sent through.
- **Otherwise, `reasoning` maps to the closest level the model supports,
rounding down.** Rounds up only when there is no lower level. A
compatibility warning is emitted whenever the value sent differs from
the one requested.
- **Rounding never goes down into `none` when reasoning was requested.**
- **Unsupported `'none'` maps to the model's lowest level.** Dropping
the value, as often done before, uses the provider's default reasoning
instead.
- **Rounding only applies to recognized models or families.** New models
in a known family get forward-compatible defaults. Unrecognized IDs get
the reasoning value sent directly because AI SDK can't guess what they
support.

### Provider-specific changes

**OpenAI**
- `providerOptions.openai.reasoningEffort` is sent unchanged instead of
being dropped when it isn't in the model's list.
- Top-level `reasoning` on known model families is rounded.
- e.g. `none` on `gpt-6-astra` now maps to `low` instead of being
dropped
- Unknown model IDs still get the value sent directly
- Chat and Responses now share one resolver instead of two copies

**Anthropic**
- Unsupported `xhigh` reasoning rounds to `high` instead of `max`
- `none` on models that only support `between_tools` now emits a
compatibility warning

**Amazon Bedrock**
- **Anthropic models:**
- `none` on models that reject disabled thinking now maps to `low`.
Before, it sent `disabled`, which those models reject
  - Unsupported `xhigh` becomes `high` instead of `max`
  - `between_tools` substitution now warns
- **OpenAI models:**
- `gpt-oss` now has its own map (`low`/`medium`/`high`), so `none`
becomes `low` instead of being skipped
- **Nova 2:** `none` sends nothing, because Nova reasoning is off unless
an effort is sent.
- **Other models:** `none` now gets the same unsupported warning as
other levels, instead of being silently skipped.

**Google**
- **Gemini 3:** `none` substitution with the minimum thinking level now
emits a warning.
- **Gemini 2.5 Pro:** `none` sends the minimum budget of 128 with a
warning. Before, it sent `thinkingBudget: 0`, which Pro rejects

**Groq**
- GPT-OSS models always reason, so `none` now maps to `low` instead of
being dropped

**Mistral**
- On low/high/max models, `medium` becomes `low` instead of `high`

**DeepSeek**
- `medium` becomes `low` instead of `high`
- `xhigh` becomes `high` instead of `max`

- `max` becomes `xhigh`

unchanged; `ElevenLabsSpeechModel` now implements the streaming

- `ElevenLabsSpeechModel.doStream()`:
- opens `wss://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/text-to-speech/{voice}/stream-input`
with `model_id`, `output_format`, and the optional query settings
(`language_code`, `enable_logging`, `inactivity_timeout`,
`sync_alignment`, `auto_mode`, `apply_text_normalization`, `seed`,
`enable_ssml_parsing`)
- sends the init message (`text: " "`, `voice_settings`,
`generation_config.chunk_length_schedule`,
`pronunciation_dictionary_locators`, and the API key as `xi-api-key`),
text messages, then `{"text":""}`

works in every runtime; the key is kept out of the reported
`request.body`
- **text parts**: the stream-input socket speaks one voice, so a part
whose `voice` differs from the call's voice errors the stream
(`InvalidArgumentError`)

end at whitespace, and LLM deltas often split words, so partial words
are held back until the next whitespace (CJK sentence punctuation also
counts; capped at 100 held code points for unspaced scripts) and the
rest is flushed at end of input

text producer (e.g. a reasoning model) does not hit the server's default

`inactivityTimeout` turns them off so the timeout you set applies.

`audio/ogg` 48 kHz); anything else is rejected. `streaming.outputFormat`
takes a native format (e.g. `mp3_44100_192`). Default `mp3_44100_128`.
